doc.title: Curtis Fuller — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Marrying dancers; Cecilia's Club; living in Washington
summary: Fuller and Golson partnered with dancers trained in Washington; they lived together in New York after a year in DC.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Didn’t you and Benny both end up…
Marrying girls. We married the first two blacks accepted to the American Ballet.

Yes, they went to the Jones Dance Company here, I don’t know the first name, the Pamela Jones Company or something. She taught all the little girls around here in the neighborhood. She taught jazz dance and ballet dance. So my wife, the first wife, went with Katherine Dunham, the late Katherine Dunham and her dance troupe. They went all over the place to Brazil and everything. Actually, I first dated Benny Golson’s wife whose mother was the bar maid across the street form the Howard Theatre. That was
Cecilia’s Club, the little bitty woman that was her mother. They were both 19 years old and there we were so we moved to New York and we all lived together. We had a long history.
So, how much time did you stay in D.C.?
A year or something, maybe. We were in and out
You were at the 7th and T world at that point. Were you playing in the clubs?
No, I just came home, too.
Yeah, off the road just to be with my girl.
